key_gap: AI computed cost concentration correctly (machining 32.3%, top-2 61.5%) and selected the right lever (offshore machining, −$12/unit, +40% margin, $4.8M/yr), but it never ran a value-mapping pass: it inferred — not derived — that tolerance lives in heat treatment + inspection, seriously weighed Alternative B (offshoring all three cells, $5.6M/yr) and dropped it on a data hint (70% tolerance-driven customers) rather than a premium test. It failed boundary discipline: no 'what happens to the premium if this cell moves' check (moving the premium cells risks ~$12.8M/yr of premium revenue against at most ~$1.5M/yr savings, an ~8:1 self-inflicted loss) and offshoring risks (single-source, +6 weeks lead time) were named but not mitigated (dual-source, audit, safety stock). The human's answer was identical on the lever and provably safe on the premium.
learning_signal: Chain decomposition is a two-pass operation: a cost pass (concentration %, margin math — machining 32.3%, top-2 61.5%) and a value pass (which activities create the premium: heat treatment + inspection at ABEC-5, 18.75% vs ~5% commodity margin). The winning lever is the cost-concentrated *commodity* cell, and premium-creating cells must be identified by the test 'what happens to the price premium if this cell moves'. Concentration alone is not a lever: lever = cost share × premium sensitivity; the pure style lands the lever (offshoring machining) and the safety boundary (keep heat treatment/inspection in-house, dual-source, audit, safety stock) as one move.
suggested_improvement: Add a WHY-stage value-mapping gate: for every top-cost activity require (1) commodity-vs-distinctive classification (purchased capability or in-house distinctive?), (2) the premium test 'what happens to price if this cell moves?', (3) linkage to customer driver data. In HOW, every alternative must carry a differentiation-impact line, and any move touching a premium-creating activity is rejected unless the premium is re-verified; in REVIEW, require a scheduled mitigation (dual-source, vendor audit, safety stock) for every selected move with supply/quality risk before declaring SOLVED.

key_gap: The human's pure chain analysis was descriptively flawless — correct concentrations (materials 23.7%, retailer share 21.1%, top-2 44.7%) and sound in-chain levers (bundle ≈ $0.9M/yr) — but it classified the retailer margin share as a structural given and the DTC startup as adjacent context ('monitor; ~30× net; outside our chain'), so it never addressed the decision the case is actually about: a 6-month window with 60% rival-closure probability on a channel-structure move that bypasses the chain's final link. The AI's G-WHY stage classified the retail share as a transferable rent, computed the EV of waiting (0.6 × lost option), and committed to the $12M bid with a diligence condition; the grader-held outcome (rival closes in month 5; online ~22% of category by month 24) validates the structural move.
learning_signal: The value chain is a snapshot: its boundary (where the chain ends) is itself a decision variable. A cost cell that is a transferable rent (retailer margin share, 21.1% of unit cost) is misread by descriptive decomposition as a fixed link; the decisive move can live outside the chain as drawn (channel/ownership-structure shift), and its timing is set by a closing window, not by chain economics. Descriptive accuracy and decision relevance can be fully decoupled: the correct decomposition produced the wrong decision because it never asked 'which cells are rents, which could be bypassed, and what would redraw the chain?'
suggested_improvement: Add a chain-boundary audit (WHY or REVIEW stage): for each link, mark cost vs rent vs bypassable, then scan context for structural shifts (new channel, private label, platform entry) with a timing/window assessment. When a structural shift is present, the decision packet must rank at least one non-chain move (acquisition, channel entry, model change) and the EV of waiting must be computed against the window's closure probability before any in-chain optimization is declared sufficient.
